items.title: Microsoft tests new privacy controls for Windows 11 desktop apps
items.description: Microsoft has begun testing new privacy controls that will let Windows 11 users choose which desktop applications can access their camera, microphone, and precise location. [...]

items.title: Unpatched Kaltura mwEmbed Flaws Could Let Remote Attackers Read Files and Run Code
items.description: The CERT Coordination Center (CERT/CC) has disclosed two unpatched vulnerabilities in Kaltura's HTML5 video player library that allow a remote, unauthenticated attacker to read arbitrary files from a server and execute code on it. The flaws, tracked as CVE-2026-19913 and CVE-2026-19912, both stem from the same unsafe deserialization in the mwEmbedLoader.php endpoint of the mwEmbed player

items.title: Imagine the SOC Without a Queue: From Alert Backlog to AI Hypothesis Engine
items.description: The SOC we've always known was built around a model that guarantees most of the alert queue will never receive analyst review. There's never time. In a traditional SOC, the typical progression follows a well-known pattern: an alert arrives; a detection engine assigns a severity score. items.title: CISA: Over 100 Internet-Exposed Water Systems Targeted in July Cyberattacks

items.title: The MFA Identity Trap: When Authentication Creates a False Sense of Security
items.description: Organizations must distinguish identity verification, authentication and threat detection, or risk successfully authenticating the attackers they are trying to stop. The post The MFA Identity Trap: When Authentication Creates a False Sense of Security appeared first on SecurityWeek.
